shift/told/s0.evidence: Round 1 states the rule outright: "the target, missing, extra and target-height channels are rolled 4 columns along x, wrapping around, but the build channels are not." Round 4 says it again: "a learned full-width circular (1,X) convolution on the target-side channels undoes the 4-column roll." It never says the roll goes toward higher x. Still, the text names which channels change, the axis, the amount and the wraparound, so it states the rule's substance.

shift/readouts/s0.evidence: Round 1 says the observed target is shifted with wraparound along x: "each row is shifted around by X/2 columns (on 8x8, the left and right halves swap; rows stay put)". It adds that "the observed target channels, and possibly the missing/extra channels" are misaligned. On an 8-wide grid that is the 4-column wrapped roll. Rounds 3–4 repeat it: "The observed target is rolled X/2 columns." Caveat: "X/2" would differ from a fixed 4 columns on grids that aren't 8 wide.

shift/scores/s0.evidence: The text never says the target channels in the observation are shifted 4 columns along x. Round 3 only guesses that "the action indices are transposed, permuted or anchored differently", which is about how actions map to cells, not about a shifted target. Round 4 drops that idea and also rules out "a permutation of observation channels". It then blames early policy collapse onto DONE. No round describes a spatial shift or wraparound of the target.

shift/hidden/s0.evidence: None of the rounds says the target observation is shifted or wrapped. Round 3 assumes the observation lines up with the build: a brick is right "only if its landing layer... matches the target cells exactly at that layer," and it worries that convolutions "may blur" per-column detail. Rounds 1–4 discuss only training settings and network designs (e.g. "n_envs to 128", "dilated residual convolution"). Nothing mentions a 4-column roll toward higher x.

mirror/told/s0.evidence: Round 1 states the rule outright: "The likely reason is the mirror rule. An action at column x places its brick at column 8-dx-x". It adds that the cells that matter "are on the mirrored side of the board" and the same row is implied. This names both what changes (where the brick lands) and how (the left-right mirror formula 8-dx-x), which matches the hidden rule.

mirror/readouts/s0.evidence: Round 1 states the rule outright: "the action's column index is mirrored relative to the observation. A brick at action column x with width dx fills observed columns X-dx-x to X-1-x. Rows and layers are as described." With X=8, the brick starts at column 8-dx-x, which matches the hidden rule exactly: a left-right mirror in the same row. Rounds 2–4 repeat that the action layout is mirrored.

mirror/scores/s0.evidence: Round 4 guesses that the action-to-cell mapping may be remapped: "If the world transposes, flips or interleaves this order... no spatially equivariant head can learn it." Round 3 also raises "a different anchor or footprint orientation." Both point to the right kind of change, a spatial remapping of where a brick lands. But neither says it is a left-right mirror within the same row, landing at column 8 - dx - x. A flip is only one option in a list of guesses.

mirror/hidden/s0.evidence: The text never says placements land at the mirrored column (8 - dx - x). Every round treats placement as happening at the chosen anchor. Round 1 explains correctness in terms of "the footprint's own columns", Round 3 says "the landing layer is the maximum height under the footprint", and Round 4 says "every cell under its footprint tops out at the same layer". None of the rounds suggests that actions are remapped or reflected.
